signal: Grofers was rebranded to Blinkit; grofer.io/grofers.com wildcards still in scope but Blinkit's own domain (blinkit.com) has no wildcard grant — strong signal of orphaned/legacy DNS records under the old brand. Check for dangling CNAMEs to decommissioned services (old CDN, S3, Heroku, etc.) once subfinder/httpx runs in a network-enabled session.
note: grofer.io (110 subs) + grofers.com (76 subs) takeover-scanned via subjack, all clean. No dangling CNAMEs found. Config-exposure hit on click.grofer.io confirmed false positive (soft-200 catch-all returning 'OK' for any path, verified with curl against a random nonexistent path).

signal: Two near-identical brand domains in scope simultaneously (ticketnew.com / tktnew.com) — classic sign of a rename/migration. Diff subdomain sets between the two; whichever is the abandoned one is the higher-value takeover target.
note: ticketnew.com (51 subs) + tktnew.com (12 subs) takeover-scanned via subjack, both clean. No dangling CNAMEs found.

signal: Program's own instruction flags zomans.com as internal AWS-hosted apps, interest = unrestricted access / internal data exposure. Prioritize this root for exposed internal tools, open S3/buckets, and auth-less admin panels — program explicitly told us this is the sensitive one.
note: zomans.com (145 subs) takeover-scanned via subjack, clean. No open S3/buckets or admin panels found via nuclei (0 findings, high/critical severity).

signal: Compare bugbounty.runnr.in against production runnr.in behavior for config drift (the 'replica' env is a common source of found-but-forgotten differences: debug endpoints, verbose errors, weaker auth).

note: UPDATE: cloud_enum sweep also flagged 'runnr.firebaseio.com' as an OPEN Firebase RTDB (unauthenticated .json read returned 8.3MB of live retailer inventory data). Investigated ownership before acting further: the data is LCBO/Wine-Rack/Beer-Store liquor inventory, matching 'Runner/Runnr' — a Toronto/Ontario, Canada alcohol delivery app, NOT Zomato's Runnr (Bengaluru hyperlocal logistics, acquired 2017, part of Eternal). Coincidental brand-name collision, unrelated company, no authorization to test it — explicitly NOT an Eternal finding. Do not pursue, do not report to Eternal's program.

evidence: http://storage.googleapis.com/zomato (public listing); object reads blocked by closed billing account
